mainTopic: שביתת כלים, the decree of שמא יחתה for food left in an oven before שבת, and giving items to a non-Jew before שבת or פסח
overview: Earlier on the דף, בית שמאי held that a Jew's utensils must 'rest' on שבת (שביתת כלים). The amud opens by explaining why they still permit incense, sulfur, a tub, a lamp, a pot and a spit: the incense sits on the ground, and the other utensils are declared הפקר. A ברייתא forbids putting raw food or a barrel of water into an oven right before שבת. The גמרא explains that even בית הלל agree, because of a rabbinic decree that a person might stoke the coals (שמא יחתה בגחלים). This decree is tested against incense, flax and wool in a dye kettle, and each is shown to be a case where stoking is unlikely or impossible. From this the גמרא draws practical rules: raw meat and fully cooked meat may be left in the oven, partly cooked meat is forbidden, and adding a raw bone makes it permitted. It then discusses kid meat versus ram meat in a sealed or unsealed oven. It records a dispute between רב אשי and רב ירמיה מדיפתי in two versions, and רבינא adds that a raw gourd is like kid meat. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה and brings ברייתות on giving items to a non-Jew before שבת and selling חמץ before פסח. רבי יהודה's view on the חמץ case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why do בית שמאי allow incense and sulfur?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בית שמאי permit leaving incense and sulfur burning into שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Incense and sulfur: what is the reason בית שמאי permitted them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. If בית שמאי say a person's utensils must rest on שבת, why do they allow incense (מוגמר) and sulfur (גפרית) to keep burning under clothes and vessels into שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, בית שמאי's view was explained through שביתת כלים: a Jew's vessel may not keep 'working' on שבת. Incense burning in a pan seems to break that rule, so the גמרא asks how בית שמאי can allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Incense burned beneath clothes to give them a pleasant scent
Sulfur, burned beneath silver vessels to whiten them
The requirement that one's utensils 'rest' on שבת

phrases.english: Incense and sulfur
phrases.notes: Placed beneath garments and silver vessels on ערב שבת

phrases.english: what is the reason Beit Shammai permitted them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about בית שמאי and שביתת כלים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the incense and sulfur cases fit with בית שמאי's rule of שביתת כלים

steps.title: The incense was placed on the ground
steps.stepSummary: The incense and sulfur sat directly on the ground, so no utensil was working.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is placed on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in those cases the incense was put straight on the ground, not inside a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שביתת כלים only applies to utensils. The ground is not a utensil, so no vessel is 'working' on שבת, and בית שמאי have no problem.

phrases.english: There, it is placed on the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The incense burned in a pan, which is a utensil
steps.terutzMaskana: The incense lay on the ground, so no utensil was involved

steps.title: Why do בית שמאי allow a tub, lamp, pot and spit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about four cases where a real utensil is clearly working into שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A tub, a lamp, a pot, and a spit: what is the reason בית שמאי permitted them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks again. These four items are definitely utensils, and each keeps working on שבת. So why do בית שמאי allow them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'it's on the ground' answer cannot work here. A fermenting tub, a burning lamp, a cooking pot, and a roasting spit are all vessels that do their job during שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A tub in which grain or fruit ferments into beer

phrases.english: A tub, and a lamp, and a pot, and a spit
what is the reason Beit Shammai permitted them?

steps.triggerLanguage: גיגית ונר וקדרה ושפוד מאי טעמא שרו בית שמאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question, applied to cases where the 'ground' answer cannot work
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How cases with real working utensils fit בית שמאי's rule

steps.title: The owner declares the utensils ownerless
steps.stepSummary: The owner makes the utensils הפקר, so they are no longer his.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he declares them fully ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the person declares these utensils ownerless (הפקר) before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שביתת כלים only applies to a Jew's own utensils. Once they are הפקר, they belong to no one, so there is no duty to let them rest.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's rule of שביתת כלים has two ways out: the item is not in a utensil (it sits on the ground), or the utensil is no longer yours (הפקר).

phrases.english: Where he declares them fully ownerless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The utensils still belong to the Jew
steps.terutzMaskana: The utensils were made הפקר, so שביתת כלים does not apply

steps.title: Who taught the ברייתא forbidding food and water left in the oven?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids putting raw pounded wheat, lupines, or a barrel of water into an oven right before שבת. The גמרא asks whether this must follow only בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught what the Rabbis taught: A woman may not fill a pot with pounded wheat and lupines and put it in the oven on ערב שבת at nightfall. If she did, even on מוצאי שבת they are forbidden for the time it takes to cook them. Similarly, a baker may not fill a barrel of water and put it in the oven on ערב שבת at nightfall. If he did, even on מוצאי שבת it is forbidden for the time it takes to cook it. Shall we say this follows בית שמאי and not בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that forbids letting food or water cook in an oven over שבת. It then asks whether this must follow בית שמאי, who forbid letting work continue into שבת, and not בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל allow starting a process before שבת and letting it finish on its own. This ברייתא forbids exactly that. So at first glance it seems to match only בית שמאי. The penalty even reaches מוצאי שבת, so the person gains nothing from the cooking done on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Lupines, a hard legume that takes long to cook
At nightfall, just before שבת begins
For the amount of time it would take to cook them
Shall we say? (introduces a suggested attribution)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the food is forbidden forever. On מוצאי שבת you only wait as long as it would take to cook it from scratch.

phrases.english: Who taught this that the Rabbis taught:
A woman may not fill a pot
with pounded wheat and lupines
and place it into the oven
on Shabbat eve at nightfall,
and if she placed them,
at the conclusion of Shabbat they are forbidden
for the time it takes for them to be cooked.
Similarly:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְמַלֵּא נַחְתּוֹם חָבִית שֶׁל מַיִם
phrases.english: a baker may not fill a barrel of water
and place it into the oven
on Shabbat eve at nightfall,
and if he did so,
at the conclusion of Shabbat it is forbidden
for the time it takes for it to be heated.
Shall we say it is Beit Shammai
and not Beit Hillel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the preceding analysis of בית שמאי and בית הלל to find the author of a new ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether this ברייתא can only follow בית שמאי

steps.title: Even בית הלל agree because of a decree about stoking coals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא can follow בית הלל too, because of a rabbinic decree that one might stir the coals on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows בית הלל: it is a decree, lest he stoke the coals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית הלל can also agree with the ברייתא. The reason here is not שביתת כלים. It is a separate rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food is not ready by nightfall, so a person might stir the coals on שבת to speed up the cooking, which is a real מלאכה. To prevent this, the Rabbis forbade putting such food in the oven just before שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a violation

steps.whyThisMatters: This decree, שמא יחתה, is the root of the הלכות of שהיה (leaving food on a fire into שבת).

phrases.english: Even if you say it is Beit Hillel,
it is a decree lest he stoke the coals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by giving a different reason for the ban
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban comes from בית שמאי's שביתת כלים
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is a decree of שמא יחתה, which בית הלל also accept

steps.title: Then decree against incense and sulfur too
steps.stepSummary: If the Rabbis fear stoking, incense and sulfur should also be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us also decree against incense and sulfur!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new decree. Incense and sulfur also burn on coals, so why weren't they forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Incense and sulfur were permitted. If the fear of stoking applies to cooking, it should apply to them as well.

phrases.english: If so,
let them also decree regarding incense and sulfur!

steps.triggerLanguage: אי הכי מוגמר וגפרית נמי לגזור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the decree of step 6 against a permitted case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The decree should apply to every case with coals, yet incense and sulfur are allowed

steps.title: Stoking would ruin the clothes and silver
steps.stepSummary: No one stokes incense or sulfur, because the smoke would damage the items.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he does not stoke them, because if he did, smoke would rise into them and harm them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a person would never stoke these coals, because the smoke would spoil the clothes and the silver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree only exists where stoking is realistic. Here stoking hurts the person's own goal, so there is no fear and no need for a decree.

phrases.english: There, they do not stoke them,
for if they stoke, smoke rises into them,
and it is harmful to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case with coals carries the fear of stoking
steps.terutzMaskana: Stoking here would cause damage, so no one would do it

steps.title: Then decree against bundles of flax
steps.stepSummary: Flax put into an oven before שבת should also be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us also decree against bundles of flax!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another permitted case. בית הלל allow flax bundles in an oven, so why not forbid them because of stoking?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flax drying in an oven seems just like food in an oven. The fear of stoking should apply here too.

phrases.english: Let them also decree regarding bundles of flax!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second test of the decree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flax in an oven is permitted, though the fear of stoking seems to apply

steps.title: Air harms the flax, so the oven stays closed
steps.stepSummary: Air damages the flax, so no one opens the oven, and no one will stoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since the air harms them, he does not uncover it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that opening the oven would let in air, which damages flax. So the person keeps it closed and will not stoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stoking requires opening the oven. Opening hurts the flax, so stoking is unlikely and no decree is needed.

phrases.english: There, since the air is harmful to them,
they do not uncover it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Flax is like food in an oven
steps.terutzMaskana: The oven stays sealed to protect the flax, so stoking will not happen

steps.title: Then decree against wool in the dye kettle
steps.stepSummary: Wool soaking in a dye kettle should also be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us decree against wool in the kettle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a third case. בית הלל allow putting wool into a dyer's kettle before שבת, so why not forbid it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dyer wants the dye to absorb well, so he might stoke the fire under the kettle. The fear seems real here.

phrases.english: Let them decree regarding wool in the kettle!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third test of the decree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wool in a heated kettle is permitted, yet the fear of stoking seems to apply

steps.title: שמואל: the kettle was taken off the fire
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the kettle was removed from the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: it is a kettle that was removed from the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that the case is a kettle already removed from the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the kettle is off the fire, there are no coals under it to stoke. So the decree does not apply.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
It refers to a kettle removed from the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The kettle sits on the fire
steps.terutzMaskana: The kettle was taken off the fire, so there are no coals to stoke

steps.title: He might still stir the kettle
steps.stepSummary: Even off the fire, he might stir the hot dye, which speeds up the cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us be concerned that he will stir it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל. Even off the fire, the person might stir the hot kettle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stirring a hot pot helps it cook, which counts as cooking (בישול). So removing the kettle from the fire solves stoking but not stirring.

phrases.english: But let us be concerned lest he stir it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's answer in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation that the kettle was removed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing it prevents stoking but not stirring, which is also forbidden

steps.title: The kettle is removed and sealed with clay
steps.stepSummary: The kettle is both off the fire and sealed shut, so stirring is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is removed and sealed with clay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the kettle is off the fire and its lid is sealed with clay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sealed kettle cannot easily be opened, so the person cannot stir it. Both worries, stoking and stirring, are now gone.
steps.whatToRemember: The decree of שמא יחתה applies only where stoking is realistic. Incense (smoke damages), flax (air damages), and a sealed kettle off the fire are all exceptions.

phrases.english: It is removed and sealed with clay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by adding a condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The kettle is removed but open
steps.terutzMaskana: The kettle is removed and sealed, so stirring is impossible

steps.title: Raw meat may be left in the oven before שבת
steps.stepSummary: Based on the decree's reason, a pot of raw meat may be put in the oven at nightfall, because no one expects to eat it that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the Master said the reason is a decree lest he stoke the coals: a pot of raw meat may be placed in the oven on ערב שבת at nightfall. Why? Since it is not fit for the night meal, he takes his mind off it and will not come to stoke the coals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a practical rule from the reason of the decree. Raw meat may be left in the oven right before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree exists because a person wants the food ready faster. Raw meat will not be ready for the Friday night meal anyway, so he forgets about it until morning. Without that urge, there is no fear of stoking.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that the Master has said (introduces a practical outcome)
He completely takes his mind off it

steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards that raw food is allowed but partly cooked food is not. Raw food is allowed because no one is in a hurry for it, so the reason for the decree does not apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known הלכה of קדרה חייתא in הלכות שהיה.

phrases.english: And now that the Master said
it is a decree lest he stoke the coals,
this pot of raw meat
is permitted to be placed
on Shabbat eve at nightfall in the oven.
What is the reason?
Since it is not fit for the evening,
he completely diverts his mind from it
and will not come to stoke the coals.

steps.triggerLanguage: והשתא דאמר מר גזירה שמא יחתה בגחלים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reason of the decree from step 6 to a practical case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pot of raw meat may be placed in the oven at nightfall on ערב שבת

steps.title: Cooked meat is allowed, half-cooked is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Fully cooked meat may be left in the oven, but partly cooked meat may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And cooked meat is permitted. Meat that is partly cooked and partly not is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more cases. Fully cooked meat is fine, but meat that is only partly cooked is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fully cooked food needs no more help, so no one will stoke. Partly cooked food is almost ready for Friday night, so the person may stoke to finish it. That is exactly the case the decree targets.

phrases.english: And cooked meat is fine.
Cooked and not cooked (partly cooked) is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the practical rulings of step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fully cooked meat is permitted; partly cooked meat is forbidden

steps.title: Adding a raw bone makes partly cooked meat permitted
steps.stepSummary: If a raw bone is added to the partly cooked pot, it may be left in the oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he threw a raw bone into it, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fix for the partly cooked pot: throw in a raw bone, and it becomes permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The raw bone will not be ready by night, so the whole pot is now meant for the next day. The person takes his mind off it, just like with raw meat, so there is no fear of stoking.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule follows the person's mindset. Raw or fully cooked means no rush, so it is permitted. Partly cooked means he wants it soon, so it is forbidden. A raw bone turns the pot back into 'for tomorrow'.

phrases.english: And if he threw a raw bone into it,
it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a way to permit the forbidden case of step 16
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Adding a raw bone to a partly cooked pot makes it like a raw pot, so it may be left in the oven before שבת

steps.title: Kid meat in a sealed oven is fine, ram meat in an unsealed oven is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Using the rule that people don't uncover food that wind harms, the גמרא lays out the two clear cases: kid meat in a sealed oven is allowed, and ram meat in an unsealed oven is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the Master said that anything wind harms, people do not uncover: kid meat in a sealed oven is fine. Ram meat in an unsealed oven is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes an earlier rule about wind and uses it to decide when raw meat may be left in an oven at nightfall on ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that a person will open the oven and stir the coals on שבת. Wind ruins kid meat, so he won't open the oven, and a clay seal blocks him even more. Ram meat isn't harmed by wind, and an open oven is easy to reach, so with neither protection it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: sealed (the oven opening, closed with clay)

steps.confusionAlert: 'שריק' describes the oven, not the meat. It means the oven's opening is sealed shut with clay.

phrases.english: And now that the Master said
anything for which wind is harmful
people do not uncover it,
this meat of a kid, with the oven sealed
is fine.
Meat of a ram, with the oven not sealed
is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the wind principle stated about flax in step 10 and applies it to the question of putting meat in the oven at nightfall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kid meat in a sealed oven is permitted. Ram meat in an unsealed oven is forbidden.

steps.title: Dispute over the mixed cases
steps.stepSummary: In the in-between cases (kid meat unsealed, or ram meat sealed), רב אשי permits and רב ירמיה מדיפתי forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: Kid meat in an unsealed oven, or ram meat in a sealed oven: רב אשי permits, and רב ירמיה מדיפתי forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now presents the two middle cases, where only one protection is present, and reports a dispute about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each middle case has one safeguard: either the meat is wind-sensitive, or the oven is sealed. רב אשי holds that one safeguard is enough. רב ירמיה מדיפתי requires both.

keyTerms.meaning: Rav Yirmeya from the town of Difti

phrases.english: Meat of a kid with the oven not sealed,
or meat of a ram with the oven sealed
Rav Ashi permits
and Rav Yirmeya from Difti forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי שָׁרֵי וְרַב יִרְמְיָה מִדִּיפְתִּי אָסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the clear cases to the disputed middle cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Middle cases: רב אשי permits, רב ירמיה מדיפתי forbids.

steps.title: Challenge to רב אשי from the teaching on roasting
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says meat may only be roasted if it can finish before nightfall. That seems to contradict רב אשי's leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב אשי, who permits: wasn't it taught that one may not roast meat, an onion, or an egg unless there is enough time for them to roast while it is still day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי with a teaching that sounds stricter than his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seems to forbid leaving any unfinished roasting meat once שבת begins. רב אשי allows it in the middle cases, so the two appear to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: but wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: And according to Rav Ashi, who permits,
wasn't it taught:
one may not roast meat, an onion, or an egg
unless there is enough time for them to roast while it is still day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lenient side of the dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's permission in the middle cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires meat to finish roasting before nightfall, with no exceptions mentioned.

steps.title: The teaching means ram meat in an unsealed oven
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא refers only to the clearly forbidden case of ram meat in an unsealed oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is talking about ram meat with the oven not sealed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב אשי by limiting the ברייתא to the case everyone agrees is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about the case with no protection at all. So it says nothing against רב אשי's leniency when one protection exists.

phrases.english: There, it is meat of a ram with the oven not sealed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids all unfinished meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא covers only ram meat in an unsealed oven.

steps.title: Second version: the dispute is only about ram meat in an unsealed oven
steps.stepSummary: According to a second version (איכא דאמרי), kid meat is always fine and sealed ram meat is fine. The dispute is only over unsealed ram meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: kid meat, whether the oven is sealed or not, is fine. Ram meat in a sealed oven is also fine. Where they argue is ram meat in an unsealed oven: רב אשי permits, and רב ירמיה מדיפתי forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, more lenient version of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here even one safeguard is enough for everyone. The argument moves to the case with no safeguard at all, which the first version called clearly forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: In this version, רב אשי is lenient even in the case the first version said was clearly forbidden.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּגַדְיָא בֵּין שְׁרִיק בֵּין לָא שְׁרִיק
phrases.english: meat of a kid, whether the oven is sealed or not sealed,
is fine.
Meat of a ram too, when the oven is sealed,
is fine.
Where they disagree is ram meat with the oven not sealed:
Rav Ashi permits
and Rav Yirmeya from Difti forbids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the dispute in a different, more lenient version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only unsealed ram meat is disputed. All other cases are permitted.

steps.title: Same challenge to רב אשי in the second version
steps.stepSummary: The roasting ברייתא is raised again against רב אשי's now even broader leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב אשי, who permits: wasn't it taught that one may not roast meat, an onion, or an egg unless there is enough time for them to roast while it is still day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same challenge, now aimed at the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the earlier answer no longer works. רב אשי permits even unsealed ram meat, so the ברייתא can't simply be about that case.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Ashi, who permits,
wasn't it taught:
one may not roast meat, an onion, or an egg
unless there is enough time for them to roast while it is still day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same challenge, applied to the alternate version.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's permission for unsealed ram meat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires roasting to finish before nightfall, which seems to conflict with leaving unsealed ram meat.

steps.title: The teaching means meat roasting directly on coals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא refers to meat roasted on open coals, not meat inside an oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is talking about meat placed on the coals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a different setup: roasting right on the coals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat sitting directly on coals invites stirring much more than meat inside an oven. So the strict ברייתא doesn't apply to ovens at all, and רב אשי's view stands.

phrases.english: There, it is meat placed directly on the coals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in the second version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a different cooking method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא applies to meat in an oven.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא applies only to roasting directly on coals.

steps.title: רבינא: a raw gourd counts like kid meat
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rules that a raw gourd may be left to cook, because wind harms it just as it harms kid meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: this raw gourd is fine. Since wind harms it, it is like kid meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא applies the wind principle to a new food, the raw gourd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wind damage is what keeps a person from opening the cooking space. Any food that wind harms gets the same leniency as kid meat.
steps.whatToRemember: The key test is whether wind harms the food. If it does, the person won't open the oven to stir the coals, so it is like kid meat.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
this raw gourd
is fine,
since wind is harmful to it,
it is like the meat of a kid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the wind principle to a new food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A raw gourd is treated like kid meat and may be left to cook.

steps.title: Giving things to a non-Jew before שבת: בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and brings a ברייתא. בית שמאי require that the גוי reach his home before שבת. בית הלל require only that he reach a house near the city wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'בית שמאי say one may not sell.' The Rabbis taught: בית שמאי say a person may not sell, lend, loan, or give an item as a gift to a גוי unless the גוי can reach his home before nightfall. בית הלל say: as long as he can reach a house next to the city wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that spells out the dispute in more detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that the גוי will carry the Jew's item on שבת, and it will look like the Jew's work. בית שמאי require the item to arrive fully at its destination before שבת. בית הלל only require it to get close, to the edge of the city.

phrases.english: (The Mishnah said:) Beit Shammai say: one may not sell.
The Rabbis taught: Beit Shammai say:
a person may not sell his item to a non-Jew,
nor lend it to him, nor loan him money,
nor give it to him as a gift
unless there is enough time for him to reach his home.
And Beit Hillel say:
enough time for him to reach a house next to the city wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a new phrase in the משנה and opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the גוי must reach his home before שבת. בית הלל: he must reach a house near the city wall.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: enough that he leaves the house
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rules it is enough if the גוי can leave the Jew's doorway before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: as long as there is time for him to leave through the doorway of the house.
steps.whatsHappening: A third, most lenient opinion is added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the item has left the Jew's home, what the גוי does with it afterward is not the Jew's concern.

keyTerms.meaning: from the doorway of his house

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
enough time for him to leave the doorway of the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, more lenient view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is enough if the גוי can leave the Jew's house before שבת.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא is only explaining בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says רבי עקיבא's view is really בית הלל's view, explained correctly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: רבי עקיבא's words are the same as בית הלל's words. רבי עקיבא only came to explain what בית הלל meant.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא clarifies that רבי עקיבא is not adding a new opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are not three opinions here, only two. The 'house near the wall' version of בית הלל was a misreading, and רבי עקיבא's 'leaving the doorway' is בית הלל's true position.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's real view, as explained by רבי עקיבא, is that the item only needs to leave the Jew's house before שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said:
these are exactly the words of Rabbi Akiva,
these are exactly the words of Beit Hillel;
Rabbi Akiva came only
to explain the words of Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinterprets רבי עקיבא's view as an explanation of בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's view is the true meaning of בית הלל.

steps.title: Selling חמץ to a non-Jew before פסח
steps.stepSummary: A parallel ברייתא: בית שמאי allow selling חמץ to a גוי only if it will be used up before פסח. בית הלל allow it as long as the Jew may still eat חמץ. רבי יהודה begins to give his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: בית שמאי say a person may not sell his חמץ to a גוי unless he knows it will be finished before פסח. These are the words of בית שמאי. בית הלל say: as long as it is permitted to eat it, it is permitted to sell it. רבי יהודה says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar dispute about חמץ, and this passage ends just as רבי יהודה starts to speak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the שבת case. בית שמאי worry about what happens to the item later, so the חמץ must be gone before פסח. בית הלל say that once it is sold while still permitted, the Jew is no longer responsible for it.

keyTerms.meaning: that it will be used up

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Beit Shammai say:
a person may not sell his chametz to a non-Jew
unless he knows about it
that it will be used up before Pesach;
these are the words of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel say:
as long as it is permitted to eat it
it is permitted to sell it.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: לֹא יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם חֲמֵצוֹ לְגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel dispute between the same schools.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: חמץ may be sold only if it will be used up before פסח. בית הלל: it may be sold as long as eating it is still permitted.
